key_insight: IncrementalExecution estimates the minimum shots needed for a fixed quantum circuit by stopping when additional executions no longer materially change the measured output distribution.
engineering_relevance: This can cut quantum runtime and cost on noisy cloud hardware by avoiding unnecessary shots while preserving a target level of result fidelity.
method: Runs shots incrementally rather than in one fixed batch.
Checks for the point of diminishing returns using the empirical output distribution.
Supports customizable shot-management policies in a black-box setting with no circuit- or noise-model assumptions.
evidence_signal: The paper reports evaluation across 33,750 framework configurations and 180 unique static circuit-backend combinations, totaling 7.3M independent experiments.
watch_item: Because the method is tuned for static circuits, its stopping behavior may need revalidation when circuits, noise conditions, or backend performance drift over time.
paper_title: How Many Shots Are Enough for a Quantum Circuit?
